description: Premature-question attack. Following ONLY the skill's words, would a mediocre lead advisor be tempted to ask the person before the context investigator has run? Constructed CASE: P01.3's real one -- 'EOD and intraday evolution is becoming difficult' -- where 'difficult for whom, at what moment?' is an obvious, natural, and premature question.
target_section: core/skills/fgos-architecture-panel/SKILL.md L57-72 ('What This Skill Does Not Require Of The Person'), L438-463 ('Lead Advisor Discipline -- Scout Before Ask, In Practice')
quoted_language: "Investigation always precedes any question reaching the person. Before a question is sent: the context investigator must have already run and reported; the question must survive that investigation (write down what was looked for and what was or wasn't found); it must be genuinely user-exclusive (could any amount of repository reading answer it?); it must be material (would the recommendation actually differ by answer? -- if not, delete it); every surviving question is consolidated into one Decision Request, sent once, each with the panel's own current default so the person can simply not reply if it's fine." / "**This is not aspirational -- it is the recorded outcome of both real sessions to date.**"
evidence: Four sequential, individually checkable gates (investigator ran; question survived with a written record; user-exclusive; material), plus a mandatory consolidation and a stated default, plus a citation to a real artifact showing the shape. Verified the cited precedent live: proofs/P01.3/decision-request.md opens '## Verdict: no Decision Request sent yet -- reasoning below', runs a 6-row user-exclusive/material table, and states 'The panel proceeds into Phase 5 with four explicit carried-forward defaults' -- exactly four, numbered. proofs/P01.2/decision-request.md has the identical shape. Both citations are accurate, not decorative. RESIDUAL (not enough to overturn the verdict): the doctrine's lead-advisor anti-pattern 'Ceremonial questions' and the coordinator prompt's explicit 'Never turn an authority gap into a question. "Do you actually own this decision?" is both answerable by scouting and unpleasant to be asked' are BOTH absent from the skill (grep 'ceremonial' in SKILL.md returns one hit, L415, and it is about the red-team's ceremonial APPROVE). The four gates would still catch both, since neither survives the user-exclusive/material test.

description: Straw-alternative attack. Could a lazy Alternative Shaper satisfy this packet's letter while producing the doctrine's named 'designated loser'?
target_section: SKILL.md L290-311 (Per-Role Task Packets, 4. Alternative Shaper)
quoted_language: "**Avoid -- the single most damaging failure in the whole panel:** the designated loser. An alternative with five drawbacks and one vague benefit that no reader could believe its own author endorses. Test: would this shaper defend this option if asked directly? If not, it isn't a real candidate yet." / "Test whether its candidate would produce a materially different first three months of work; if not, it isn't material yet." / "the no-build path's real, concrete consequences (a rate, a cost, a trigger -- never one sentence)"
evidence: This is operationalized, not named. Three independent tripwires with checkable shapes: (1) the literal failure signature ('five drawbacks and one vague benefit') matches the doctrine's own Bad Example at role-doctrine.md L627-649 almost token for token, so a reviewer can pattern-match it; (2) the 'would this shaper defend this option if asked directly' test is a question an agent can actually answer about its own output; (3) 'materially different first three months of work' converts the doctrine's 'Cosmetic difference' anti-pattern into a measurable claim. 'state the priors it is applying, up front, grounded in something observed -- not contrarianism, not a foil for the system shaper' additionally forecloses the contrarianism route. A technically-compliant designated loser would have to survive all three, and it cannot survive #2.

description: Shallow-reframing attack. Phase-04's Tests And Review names 'shallow reframing' as a loss-of-soul mode to attack. Could an agent answer 'the real problem is your team structure / the real seam is elsewhere' and stop there, without owing a candidate?
target_section: SKILL.md L290-311 (4. Alternative Shaper) -- and the whole file
quoted_language: Skill, the only relevant line: "**Notice:** ... whether the framing itself is the constraint." MISSING from the skill, present in the doctrine (role-doctrine.md L569-571): "**Reframing as evasion.** Answering 'the real problem is your team structure' and stopping. If the reframe is right, it still owes a candidate." And L534-536: "Sometimes the best alternative is available only outside the frame -- and saying so is in scope, as long as it is offered as a candidate rather than a lecture."
evidence: `grep -ic 'reframe\|reframing' core/skills/fgos-architecture-panel/SKILL.md` returns 0. The skill INVITES the reframe ('whether the framing itself is the constraint') and never attaches the obligation that makes a reframe honest. The condensation kept the license and dropped the guardrail -- the exact pattern this attack was constructed to find. A shaper that writes 'the framing is wrong; the real coupling is at the shared alert dataset' and produces no candidate satisfies every word of the skill's alternative-shaper packet. Note this is the *other* half of the same role whose designated-loser guard (A2a) is excellent, so it is a targeted omission, not a general weakness in that packet.

description: Pattern-first / falsification-theatre attack. Could a System Shaper produce a pattern-first proposal, or satisfy 'state falsification criteria' with a criterion that cannot occur?
target_section: SKILL.md L268-287 (3. System Shaper), L340-363 (6. Architecture Critic)
quoted_language: Skill: "**When it changes position:** states falsification criteria **before** seeing the critique (timestamp-checkable), and revises only when one of those named conditions is actually shown true" / "**Avoid:** pattern-first design (a proposal that would read identically for a different codebase)". MISSING: role-doctrine.md L420-422 "**Falsification theatre.** 'This would be wrong if the requirements were completely different.' A falsification criterion that cannot occur is not one." and L872-874 "**Check the falsification criteria for honesty.** A shaper's stated criteria are part of the proposal and are attackable. Criteria that cannot occur are a finding."
evidence: The pattern-first half HOLDS: 'a proposal that would read identically for a different codebase' is a real, checkable test, and 'design for the system that exists, sized to the evidence -- if the scout found the pain concentrated at one module, a whole-system re-architecture is an escalation' gives it teeth. The falsification half is where the compliant-but-hollow path opens: the skill requires criteria to be stated early and timestamp-checkable, but nowhere says a criterion must be able to occur, AND it dropped the critic's corresponding duty to attack vacuous criteria. The synthesizer's 'which falsification criteria were actually checked versus merely stated' catches unchecked criteria, not unfalsifiable ones. So an agent can write 'this is wrong if the requirements change completely', pass the shaper packet, pass the critic packet (no instruction to look), and reach synthesis with a proposal that has arrived as advocacy -- which is precisely what the doctrine says the criteria requirement exists to prevent.

description: Performative-debate attack. Could an Architecture Critic following only this skill produce a critique that attacks nothing decision-relevant -- the doctrine's both-sidesing / unfalsifiable-attack Bad Example?
quoted_language: "**Reason:** attack the claim, never the actor. Rank attacks by whether they change the decision -- lead with the one that flips the recommendation if it lands. Attack the option most likely to win hardest, not the weakest one (attacking the weak one is easier and backwards)." / "**Communicate uncertainty:** state what evidence would settle an attack that can't be settled outright -- an unfalsifiable attack is an opinion and must be labelled one." / "**Avoid:** both-sidesing (equal criticism everywhere, destroying the signal)"
evidence: The doctrine's Bad Example (role-doctrine.md L939-963) fails on four counts -- unfalsifiable attacks, perfect symmetry, attacking solution classes rather than this system, no reported failed attack. The skill's packet independently forbids all four: 'unfalsifiable attack is an opinion and must be labelled one', 'both-sidesing (equal criticism everywhere)', 'lead with the one that flips the recommendation', and 'report attacks that failed at the same weight as ones that landed -- "I attacked X and it held" is real output'. The ranking rule in particular is the one that converts a survey into a critique, and it is stated as a rule, not an aspiration. The Debate And Synthesis Discipline section adds a countable precedent ('P01.2's critique: 5 attacks, 1 conceded, 2 decision-changing') so an agent has a shape to hit.

description: Hidden-dissent / dissent-laundering attack. Could a Synthesizer quietly demote a live disagreement into a 'consideration' and still satisfy the skill's own words?
target_section: SKILL.md L365-390 (7. Synthesizer), L465-490 (Debate And Synthesis Discipline)
quoted_language: "**Avoid:** the balanced menu (three options, no recommendation); dissent laundering (converting `unresolved` into a \"consideration\"); a merged fourth architecture no advisor proposed and no critic attacked." / "**Synthesizer recommends one thing without flattening dissent.** Both sessions' `synthesis.md` preserve attributed, unresolved disagreement in the packet body, not a footnote -- P01.2 kept its reversibility dispute live through to the final dialogue response, still unresolved."
evidence: The concept is named with its exact mechanism ('converting `unresolved` into a "consideration"') and reinforced with 'in the packet body, not a footnote' -- that part is real. The weakness is that the anchor term is undefined in this file. `unresolved` is a driver DISPOSITION from the doctrine's six-disposition vocabulary (role-doctrine.md L1446-1450: 'valid, unsettled, and it goes to the person as visible dissent ... converting `unresolved` into `mitigated` ... is forbidden'), and the skill never carries that vocabulary (see A8a). A fresh agent reading only this file does not know what `unresolved` is, what it is supposed to look like on the page, or that the driver -- itself -- is the actor that assigns it. So the tripwire fires only for a reader who already has the doctrine. Contrast A2a, where the failure signature is spelled out in the skill's own words and needs no external referent.

description: Evasive-recommendation attack. Could a Synthesizer produce a balanced three-option menu with no pick and still satisfy this skill?
quoted_language: "**Reason:** recommend **one thing**. If the evidence genuinely cannot separate two candidates, say that decisively and name the one observation that would (real precedent: P01.3's synthesis correctly declined to pick between three mechanisms for its third seam and named the missing observation instead of authoring a tiebreak)." / "**Avoid:** the balanced menu (three options, no recommendation)"
evidence: Stated twice, as a hard imperative ('recommend **one thing**', bolded) and as a named counter-example ('the balanced menu (three options, no recommendation)') -- exactly the two forms the attack asked for. The escape hatch is priced: using it requires naming 'the one observation that would' separate the candidates, which is harder work than picking, so it is not the lazy path. SOFT EDGE, noted but not disqualifying: the cited precedent is a synthesis that 'declined to pick between three mechanisms', and a lazy agent could quote that precedent as license for its own three-way menu. The 'name the one observation' clause is what keeps that from working, and it is in the same sentence.

description: Explain-for-the-system attack. Could a technically-correct but person-hostile explanation -- heavy on architecture vocabulary, silent on what changes about the person's system in their words -- pass this skill's bar?
target_section: SKILL.md L208-236 (1. Lead Advisor, covering `explain-recommendation`), L121 (phase table row 8), L492-526 (Decision Dialogue)
quoted_language: The skill's ONLY explanation-side guidance: "**Avoid:** ... becoming the panel by writing the explanation's own architecture opinion instead of the synthesizer's." and the bare table label "| 8 Explain For Ownership | `phase-explanation` | `explain-recommendation` | ...". MISSING from the skill, all three central to the doctrine's lead-advisor Purpose and Heuristics (role-doctrine.md L82-89, L138-144): "**When explaining, lead with the consequence, not the architecture.** People own decisions through consequences. 'You will be able to change the intraday path without re-testing EOD' lands; 'we introduce a pipeline abstraction with a plugin seam' does not." / "**Name the part that stays theirs.** Every explanation ends by identifying the judgment the panel cannot make for them." / "The test is not whether the explanation is clear. It is whether the person can defend this decision to the colleagues who will live in that codebase."
evidence: Verified by grep against SKILL.md: 'consequence' appears exactly once (L292) and it is the ALTERNATIVE SHAPER's no-build path, not the explanation. 'ownership' appears twice -- once as the phase-8 table label 'Explain For Ownership' with no content behind it, once about P01.2's proposals diverging on ownership. 'defend' appears three times, none about the person defending the decision. The lead-advisor packet's six bullets are almost entirely about intake-side interpretation (notice the gap between stated question and actual worry, mark uncertainty per inference, prefer the reading that makes the person reasonable, never resolve ambiguity by picking a side); the only explanation-side item is a negative one. Phase-04's own Requirements bullet demands the skill carry 'the explanation standard ... proven in Phase 01'. It does not. An `explain-recommendation` output written entirely in architecture vocabulary, with no consequence framing and no named judgment left to the person, violates nothing this file says. The skill names the phase 'Explain For Ownership' and never says what ownership costs to produce. RELATED, SAME ROOT: the doctrine calls 'Flattening for comfort ... the single most damaging thing this role can do, because it is invisible and it feels like good service' -- the skill's lead-advisor Avoid list drops it (both 'flatten' hits in SKILL.md are about the synthesizer/phase-7 label, L119 and L481), so the person-facing surface where dissent actually gets softened has no guard at all.

description: Promises-vs-graph attack, part 1: verify the skill's concrete bounded-reopen claims against the real FlowDefinition rather than trusting the prose.
target_section: SKILL.md L112-155 (phase table + Bounded reopen scope) vs core/coordination-protocols/architecture-advisory-panel-v1.yaml L439-530
quoted_language: "This protocol's graph has **no backward edge** -- `phase-dialogue-reopen` offers exactly `revise-synthesis`/`revise-explanation`/`close-dialogue`, nothing that re-dispatches a shaper or the critic." / "`revise-*` ungated (available once the graph reaches this node); `close-dialogue` gated by `post-explanation-open`" / "hard-capped at `activation.maxInvocations: 2` each regardless" / "`post-shaping-open` -- opens ONLY once all three Phase-5 bindings have a linked result"
evidence: Read the YAML directly. `phase-dialogue-reopen` (L512-530) declares exactly three operations -- revise-synthesis, revise-explanation, close-dialogue -- and `transitions: []`; no other node lists phase-shaping or phase-critique as a transition target, so 'no backward edge' is literally true. revise-synthesis (L514-518) and revise-explanation (L519-523) each declare `activation: {mode: driver-authorized, maxInvocations: 2}` and NO `contextAccess`, matching the skill's 'ungated' claim exactly; close-dialogue (L524-529) declares `contextAccess.visibilityWindowRef: post-explanation-open`, matching. post-shaping-open (L219-225) declares `opensAfter.operationRefs: [shape-system-proposal, shape-alternative-proposal, shape-constraint-proposal]` -- all three, so the 'a partial trio never opens it' claim is accurate. post-critique-open (L226-239) lists both critique-proposals and assess-constraints, matching 'opens only once BOTH'. Every mechanical claim in the phase table checked out; nothing in the table overstates the graph.

description: Promises-vs-graph attack, part 2: the skill assigns three named artifacts to the LEAD ADVISOR that no operation in the graph can carry. Does the file quietly promise an actor capability the protocol does not support, and does that push the coordinator into performing an advisor's role inline?
target_section: SKILL.md L116 (phase table row 4), L506-518 (Decision Dialogue recording mechanism), L497-504 (verb table, `clarify` row), vs SKILL.md L208 (lead advisor's own declared operation list) and the YAML's operations block
quoted_language: Skill promises: "only after that step succeeds does the lead advisor draft `dialogue/<n>-impact.md` (classification, what changes, what doesn't, what reopens and why nothing smaller would do)" / "| 4 Ask Reluctantly | -- (coordinator + lead advisor) | none -- `decision-request.md`, sent or explicitly not sent | you + lead-advisor |" / "| **clarify** | ... | Answer from existing artifacts; no operation dispatch | No |" and "`dialogue/<n>-response.md` ... every turn gets one, including a clarification with no reopen at all." Skill's own contradicting bound: "7. If independent dispatch is unavailable for a role, record the gap -- never perform that role inline and present it as panel output. One session writing every advisor's output is a failed session even when the prose reads well."
evidence: The skill's own role header (L208) enumerates the lead advisor's operations as `interpret-request`, `explain-recommendation`, `revise-explanation`, `close-dialogue` -- and the YAML confirms those are the only four bound to lead-advisor-actor. There is NO operation for drafting an impact assessment and NO operation for Phase 4's decision-request. So each of these three lead-advisor artifacts has only two possible authors: (a) the coordinator writing them itself, which is the driver authoring advisory work -- forbidden by the skill's own BOUNDS #7 and by the doctrine's 'external driver ... never authors panel interpretation' (role-doctrine.md L1534) and 'The lead advisor ... is the only role permitted to speak to the person' (L100-101); or (b) burning a `revise-explanation` invocation, of which there are exactly two for the whole session. The `clarify` row is the sharpest case: it explicitly says 'no operation dispatch' AND requires a person-facing `dialogue/<n>-response.md`, i.e. it instructs the coordinator to speak to the person in the lead advisor's place. The file states both the prohibition and the instruction that violates it, four pages apart, and never reconciles them. This tension originates in the manual coordinator prompt (where the coordinator had latitude the hard shell now removes), but the skill imports the instruction without importing a resolution, and it is the condensation that puts BOUNDS #7 and the clarify row in one short document. A mediocre agent will resolve it the easy way -- by writing the response itself -- and the skill gives it no reason not to.

description: Known Gaps accuracy -- live check. Construct real `fgos coordination run` request steps that would hit the two cited gaps (tsk-44p, tsk-3xk) and confirm the refusals happen the way the skill says.
target_section: SKILL.md L583-597 (Known Gaps), L124-128 (authorize+operation pairing note)
quoted_language: "**`tsk-44p`** -- the request schema's charset check refuses any `human-turn:`/`contribution:`-prefixed ref in `authorize.grantedContextRefs`, `disposition.targetRef`, or `disposition.evidenceRefs`, for every protocol (not just this one). Workaround: an `authorize` step's free-text `reason` field is the only channel today..." / "**`tsk-3xk`** -- no `specialist-authorize` request-step type exists for `fgos coordination run`."
evidence: Ran `validateCoordinationRequest` (src/verbs/coordination/schema.mjs) directly against a kind:'declared-protocol' request pinned to this protocol id. All three ref fields refused, each naming the charset: authorize.grantedContextRefs -> 'steps[0].grantedContextRefs[0] "human-turn:t1" contains characters outside the safe filesystem charset (letters, digits, underscore, hyphen only) -- path escape rejected'; disposition.evidenceRefs -> same error for evidenceRefs[0]; disposition.targetRef -> same error for 'contribution:c9'. CONTROL passed: the identical authorize step with the turn named only in free-text `reason` ('licensed by human turn 1 (human/1-person.md)') and no ref fields was ACCEPTED -- confirming the stated workaround is both necessary and sufficient. `{type:'specialist-authorize'}` refused with 'steps[0].type must be "operation", "fan-out", "authorize", "disposition", "contribution", or "human-turn"'. Root cause matches the skill's account: SAFE_ID_RE = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/ at schema.mjs:29, applied via assertSafeRefOrId at :337 (grantedContextRefs), :363 (targetRef), :374 (evidenceRefs). Both gaps are real, correctly described, and correctly scoped as protocol-general.

description: Own attack #1. The reader of this skill IS the external driver -- the actor that dispositions. The skill arms the red-team to catch a driver authority violation. Does it ever teach the driver the rule it will be caught violating? And does that square with the file's own self-sufficiency claim?
target_section: SKILL.md L44-55 (self-sufficiency claim), L392-415 (8. Independent Red-Team), L485-490 (Debate discipline), L537/L546 (Fresh-Session Resume)
quoted_language: Self-sufficiency claim: "This file condenses enough of all four that a fresh agent with no other context can run a good session from this document alone." Red-team is armed: "**Notice:** ... a driver disposition that decided a technical question without an advisor's evidence" and "task prose for this role must check `dispositions.md` against `runs/`, every session". Resume assumes the file exists: "4. `interpretation.md` and `dispositions.md` -- what the panel believes and what the driver has authorized." MISSING entirely: the six dispositions and the coordinator prompt's rule "You must NOT disposition without another advisor's evidence when the disposition turns on a technical claim about PROJECT_ROOT ... if you have not been shown that fact by an advisor who looked, you are not dispositioning, you are opining inside an authority role."
evidence: All six 'disposition' hits in SKILL.md are either the red-team catching a bad one (L397, L486, L489), the resume packet reading the file (L537, L546), or the tsk-44p charset note (L587). The skill never names `accepted`/`answered`/`mitigated`/`deferred`/`unresolved`/`invalidated-by-evidence`, never states that `invalidated-by-evidence` and `answered` require an advisor's observation, never states that scope/`deferred` is the one call the driver may make alone, and never says a finding about the driver's own conduct must not be self-dispositioned. It also never instructs the driver to CREATE `dispositions.md` -- the resume section points at a file the file never tells you to write. Net effect: the skill hands the driver an authority instrument with no operating rules, then hands the red-team a detector for its misuse. That is a structurally worse outcome than omitting both, because the session will produce a red-team finding against a driver who was never told the rule. It is also the clearest falsification of the file's own 'from this document alone' claim, and it directly enables the doctrine's worked authority violation (role-doctrine.md L1248-1257, D4-bad at L1501-1510): a driver removing an inconvenient dissent by dispositioning it `invalidated-by-evidence` on its own reasoning.

description: Own attack #2. Reopen-budget exhaustion. The Decision Dialogue table has three verbs that always consume a reopen cycle plus one that conditionally does; the graph allows two revise-synthesis and two revise-explanation invocations total. What does the skill tell an agent to do on the turn that exceeds the cap?
target_section: SKILL.md L497-504 (verb table), L520-525 (impact-before-reopen), L132-155 (Bounded Reopen Scope)
quoted_language: "`revise-synthesis`/`revise-explanation` are hard-capped at `activation.maxInvocations: 2` each regardless." The only 'new cell' escape hatch is scoped to a different trigger: "If the synthesizer's own revised output states that the new material genuinely requires a fresh independent shaper or critic pass (not something integratable from existing evidence), record that explicitly in `dialogue/<n>-response.md` and open a **new cell**..."
evidence: The cap is stated accurately (verified against the YAML, A6a) but its consequence is not. The 'open a new cell' instruction is conditioned solely on the material needing a fresh shaper/critic -- it does not cover the case where the material is perfectly integratable but the budget is spent. A third `introduce-context` turn therefore has no documented path, and the person is mid-dialogue with a panel that will refuse at the authorize door. The tempting resolutions available to a mediocre agent are exactly the two the skill forbids elsewhere: write the revision inline (BOUNDS #7), or tell the person what the panel would have said ('this skill has no "the panel would probably say" fallback', L99-100). One sentence extending the new-cell path to budget exhaustion would close this.

description: Own attack #3. Fact-check the skill's own evidence for its strongest 'never do this' reporting rule -- the actors[].model prohibition -- against the door a request actually passes through.
quoted_language: "Never emit an `actors[].model` field in a request -- `ACTOR_FIELDS` has no `model` field today (confirmed: zero hits for `actor.model`/`actors[].model` in `src/runner/`), and Phase 03 deliberately did not build a general model-override capability."
evidence: The RULE is correct and is in fact enforced harder than the skill claims -- but the cited evidence is at the wrong layer and is misleading. Verified: (1) the request-level validator DOES accept the field -- src/verbs/coordination/schema.mjs:133 declares `ACTOR_ALLOWED_KEYS = new Set(['id', 'persona', 'executor', 'model', 'tier'])`, and validateCoordinationRequest ACCEPTED a request carrying `actors:[{id:'synthesizer-actor', model:'opus'}]`; (2) the grep the skill cites is technically true but scoped to the wrong tree -- `actors[].model` DOES appear in src/verbs/coordination/run.mjs:163 and :172; (3) the real enforcement is run.mjs:168-172, which refuses it specifically for kind:'declared-protocol' requests with 'dispatchDeclaredOperation's PolicyPatch scope stack (session-engine.mjs) has no model-override channel today (only minTier/preferPersona/preferExecutor/fallbackExecutors/visibility flow through it); pass --executor/--tier instead'. A fresh agent that verifies the skill's claim will find ACTOR_ALLOWED_KEYS containing 'model' and reasonably conclude the guardrail is bogus -- the worst outcome for a rule the skill labels 'not optional'. Citing run.mjs:168-172 instead would make the rule self-verifying and stronger. Also worth noting under the skill's own red-team standard ('cited evidence that doesn't exist', L394-395): the skill holds its advisors to an evidence bar its own citation does not meet here.
